headline: Philly spends on the Eagles first, and a Sixers jersey is a loyalty statement
summary: Clothing is tax-free on both sides of the river, so the sticker is the price. The Eagles set the retail calendar, and Sixers spending bunches up at tip-off, the holidays and playoff runs. Incomes run from price-sensitive North and West Philly to the wealthy Main Line and Center City, so the good-better-best ladder has to be clear. LeBron and Brown bring a rare mid-cycle jersey surge.

insights.title: Clothing is tax-free on both sides of the river
insights.detail: Pennsylvania doesn't tax most clothing or footwear, and New Jersey exempts both too. Delaware has no sales tax at all. The Delaware Valley has no back-to-school tax weekend and no tax-holiday spike, because none is needed. Philadelphia's local add-on applies to taxable goods, not to jerseys and tees.
insights.implication: Don't build promotions around tax savings. Compete on price points, bundles and exclusivity. Footwear and apparel launches price the same in Philly and the suburbs, so one tier ladder works across the region.

insights.title: Eagles season crowds out the NBA
insights.detail: From September to January the city's wallet and wardrobe go Eagles green, and Phillies October runs do the same when they happen. Sixers spending clusters around opening night, Christmas gifting and the playoffs instead of building steadily.
insights.implication: Launch Sixers product in the October window, with a second beat in early December for gifting. Don't fight Eagles weekends for attention. Keep playoff-run drops ready to turn around fast.

insights.title: New stars mean a mid-cycle jersey reset
insights.detail: LeBron James and Jaylen Brown are newly in Sixers blue alongside Embiid, Maxey and Edgecombe, so fans have to pick a name to wear. Opening night at the Knicks and Christmas Day at the Lakers are both high-attention national games.
insights.implication: Stock depth across several player jerseys and name-and-number tees instead of betting on one. Replenish James and Brown fast, and watch for health-driven swings in Embiid demand.

insights.title: Wide income spread, strong value instinct
insights.detail: In North and West Philly, a $120 to $130 swingman is a considered purchase. Main Line and Center City buyers pay for authentic and limited items. Outlet, discount and resale shopping are normal, with no stigma.
insights.implication: Tier clearly: accessible tees and hoodies, mid-price swingman and kids, and a premium authentic and collab layer. Make value visible with bundles, kids sizing and durable fabric.

insights.title: Weather makes it a layers-and-hoodies season
insights.detail: Philadelphia winters are cold and damp, with an Eagles-style outerwear culture, and summers are humid. The Sixers season runs from late fall to spring, so from November to March warm-up layers, hoodies and puffers sell as much as jerseys.
insights.implication: Pair every jersey story with a layering piece: shell jacket, hoodie, beanie. Save short-sleeve shooting shirts for the playoffs and summer league.

insights.title: Gifting and resale shape the premium end
insights.detail: Holiday gifting runs hard from Black Friday to Christmas. Long-running local sneaker chains like Sneaker Villa, plus online resale, carry the demand for hyped footwear and colorways.
insights.implication: Use limited footwear and apparel drops to feed the local sneaker conversation. Keep quantities controlled to limit resale arbitrage on team-tied items.

insights.title: Shoppers cross state lines
insights.detail: South Jersey, Delaware and the Pennsylvania suburbs shop at King of Prussia, Cherry Hill and Philadelphia Mills as readily as Center City. Game-day buyers shop at the arena complex in South Philadelphia.
insights.implication: Plan distribution around the mall and outlet nodes and the arena pro shop, not only city-core flagships. Expect suburban families to buy kids and gift items.

places.name: Xfinity Mobile Arena
places.why: The home arena, and the place most likely to close a team-merchandise sale on game day. A new arena is planned on the former Spectrum site for about 2030.

places.name: King of Prussia Mall
places.why: The region's biggest shopping destination, pulling suburban and out-of-state shoppers in gifting season.

places.name: Philadelphia Mills
places.why: A value-minded shopping node for price-conscious families.

places.name: Fashion District Philadelphia
places.why: A central, transit-served hub where tourists and local teens overlap.

places.name: Cherry Hill Mall
places.why: Home base for South Jersey fans, who treat Philly as their team and shop close to home.

places.name: Sneaker Villa
places.why: A long-running local chain that anchors the footwear and streetwear shopper.

places.name: Walnut Street shopping corridor
places.why: A higher-income, tourist-heavy strip where premium and brand-store experiences land.

people.name: Allen Iverson
people.why: The city's retail icon. Throwback and Iverson-era product still sells and signals real fandom.

people.name: Joel Embiid
people.why: The face of the franchise. His health shapes demand, and jersey and team-apparel sales track his availability. His footwear deal is reportedly not Nike (verify).

people.name: Tyrese Maxey
people.why: A fan favorite who feels homegrown, and a durable jersey seller for younger buyers.

people.name: LeBron James
people.why: Global jersey and product demand arrives with him. He is a Nike athlete.

people.name: Jaylen Brown
people.why: A second high-interest name-and-number option for fans.

people.name: Meek Mill
people.why: A local cultural gatekeeper whose co-sign carries weight with streetwear buyers.

moments.name: NBA opening night at the Knicks
moments.why: A national NBC game that kicks off the season-launch merchandise push.

moments.name: Black Friday to Christmas gifting
moments.why: The peak gifting window for jerseys, hoodies and kids apparel.

moments.name: Christmas Day at the Lakers
moments.why: A national broadcast and James's return game, with gift-driven jersey interest.

moments.name: Mummers Parade
moments.why: A uniquely Philadelphian New Year's tradition, and a source of color and costume cues.

moments.name: Odunde Festival
moments.why: One of the country's largest African American street festivals, and a major cultural and retail moment in South Philadelphia.

moments.name: Wawa Welcome America
moments.why: A summer civic celebration that draws tourists and locals, and demand for red, white and blue.

moments.name: Playoffs
moments.why: Demand for fast-turn tees and caps spikes with every series win.

designCues.cue: Sixers royal blue as the dominant ground color
designCues.use: The lead color for accessible tees and hoodies, so the product reads as team loyalty at a glance.
Trim, number outlines and hits on outerwear.

designCues.cue: Deep navy for premium and cold-weather layers
designCues.use: Premium authentic pieces, shell jackets and beanies.
Draw on the franchise's origin in graphics and Specter stories. Skip Liberty Bell or Independence Hall imagery unless licensing is checked.

designCues.cue: Mummers sequin and feather color palette
designCues.use: Festive, high-contrast accents for gifting-season drops. If you reference specific costume designs, credit and partner with Mummers clubs.
Warm-up and travel layers for the November to March buying window.

productHooks: Opening-week tee and hoodie capsule at accessible prices, with LeBron, Brown, Embiid and Maxey name-and-number options.
The 76ers 'Specter' collection, extended into gifting-season outerwear and layers.
A kids and youth swingman bundle, priced for suburban and city families in the holiday window.
A limited footwear drop through local sneaker retailers and the arena shop, with quantities controlled to blunt resale.
A fast-turn playoff tee and cap program, launched within days of each series win.
watchouts: Don't promise tax savings. Clothing is already exempt in Pennsylvania and New Jersey, so promos have to stand on price.
Player-heavy jersey inventory carries injury and roster risk (Embiid's health, James's age). Don't make deep single-name bets.
Liberty Bell, Independence Hall and other civic imagery can need licensing or permission. Check before use.
Credit and pay Black-led institutions and creators (for example Odunde-related partners). Don't borrow the festival's cultural cues.

extra.priceProfile: Many households watch every dollar, and outlet, discount and resale shopping are normal. Affluent Main Line, Center City and South Jersey buyers pay for authentic and limited product. Tier it as accessible tees and hoodies, mid-price swingman and kids, and a premium authentic and collab layer. Clothing and footwear are exempt from sales tax in Pennsylvania and New Jersey, so the sticker price is the real price.
extra.jerseyBehavior: The swingman is the default jersey, kids and youth sizes are for families, and authentic is for the affluent core. Name-and-number choice is a loyalty statement that shifts quickly with roster news, so expect splits among Embiid, Maxey, James and Brown. Knockoff and street-vendor product shows up around game days, so authentic detailing and price-accessible options matter. Throwback Iverson-era pieces sell as heritage.
